> A musical Solid-State Tesla Coil (SSTC). The project will use a microcontroller (ESP32) to process MIDI signals and modulate a PWM signal. This signal will control a bridge of power transistors, generating high-voltage arcs that reproduce audible sound frequencies in the air, effectively transforming electricity directly into music.

## Design

### 2026-10-22 – Session Journal: Schematic Design for Solid State Tesla Coil

**10h**

Session Journal: Schematic Design for Solid State Tesla Coil
In this session, I started designing the schematic for the Solid State Tesla Coil (SSTC) using KiCad. The focus was on the power distribution and the main control circuit.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/a8e45083275c2ee696d3aca8c9367b8fff083608b34c04ac73ce51ad4bbf10ab.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/974e1d5800f35fa11c36c1d43bae8bb0470a504d493c7c7e8e5e1f63504f3870.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/706e470bc9cce16c0b8343eda8eead7f5d16452a8580151c6d64a04791d72963.png)
First, I routed the main 24V input and added an L7812 voltage regulator to provide a stable 12V line for the gate driver
Next, I added a connection for an LM2596 buck converter module to step down the 24V line to 5V.

To ensure signal stability and prevent high-frequency noise from the 24V line from interfering with the ESP32, I added filtering capacitors across the power rails.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/0ad36dac43fbf0dcb2fac9d666b35bb993d29af0d3138a71666cf7e9cb605b89.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/459257beeff9abcc57a7328817c9bff6d3e7c3df964cbc6e258e33a9a7c23ee3.png)
After setting up the power rails, I placed the main microcontroller, which is an ESP32-C3-DevKitM-1.

To isolate the microcontroller from the high-power section and to drive the MOSFET effectively, I added a TLP250 optocoupler.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/ed88a3bc93fbe228f1acd377c931be433e58302b9740a021f8d72822edc67c6e.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/T4VNKFYucNS23P2qnOKuArH2j1qOxcfx/5846a3b1f5b01307ff578be64ad7b1747b9bac0a22865268b107e0dd24eb2833.png)
Finally, I incorporated the main switching MOSFET and the connector for the primary coil wires, completing the core driving logic for the coil.

Here is the complete overview of the schematic progress made during this session.
